messages.subject: Species covariate in single-season occupancy model
parts:
Hi all!

I am interested in stacking my detection histories of 5 different species on top of each other and using "species" as a covariate to understand species-specific differences in detection and occupancy, but I'm a little unsure of how to do this. I am getting massive SEs when I try to incorporate the species covariate. Any thoughts/suggestions on this?

Mira

I have 40 cameras placed at 10 sites, 2 in "shore" habitat at each site and 2 in "inland" habitat. I have pooled the data from the shore and inland cameras, so I have 20 camera stations total. It's a low sample size but it's what I have to work with! Because of my low sample size I was hoping that combining the detection histories for the 5 species I'm interested in and running the models with a species covariate would increase my power because the 5 species could share all the other covariates? 

I have 400 rows of data, however, because each of the 5 species has 80 rows in their detection histories. Without getting too much into my study design, each camera station receives a treatment and a control during 3 months of summer, and the order in which they receive either treatment or control is reversed in the following year. So each species has 40 rows in their detection histories per summer, and there were two summers of data. 

Here is the summary from using species as an occupancy covariate (i've bolded the SEs):

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Species covariate in single-season occupancy model
parts:
You’re modeling whether at least one species is present as a function of whether at least one species is detected.
It’s inestimable, but maybe this isn’t what you are trying to do?
